title: PSK Gate System
summary: A race-timing gate for athletes at stadium tracks, taken from schematic and layout through client validation to 12 delivered units.

sections.overview: A race-timing gate for athletes at stadium tracks, built for a client at ELKO EP. He owned the electronics end to end: schematic, 2-layer PCB, prototype, client validation and assembly of the production run.
objectives: Remove the sunrise IR interference seen in the client's earlier system.
Keep the 12 V sensors electrically separate from the 3.3 V Raspberry Pi logic.
Make the sensors and the handheld button easy to unplug and replace.
sections.problem: The client's earlier system picked up IR interference at sunrise.
sections.solution: Switching to a red-LED sensor removed the interference. Two Optex CDD-100N-R sensors per gate feed a logic stage that confirms each crossing.
sections.architecture: The sensors run from 12 V, with a 5 V internal rail and 3.3 V Raspberry Pi logic. An optocoupler isolates the sensor side from the Pi. The sensors and the handheld button connect over USB Type-C into one enclosure.
sections.pcb: A 2-layer PCB designed in Altium Designer.
sections.testing: Prototype first, then client validation, then assembly of 12 units in 3 weeks.
sections.results: All 12 units work, and the client has requested further development.

title: Dual-Axis Solar Tracker
summary: Simulink model of a solar tracker with battery charging, plus the 2-layer PCB for the same power chain.

image.alt: 3D render of the dual-axis solar tracker PCB

status: Simulation stage (model-in-the-loop). Hardware not yet validated.

sections.overview: A model-based design study of a small dual-axis solar tracker with Li-ion battery charging. The reference system has a 6 W PV panel, a single 3 Ah Li-ion cell and a 5 V load. He also designed the 2-layer PCB for the same power chain.
objectives: Model the full power chain: PV panel, charger, protection and boost stage.
Add position control so the panel follows the sun.
Design the PCB around the same chain, with monitoring.
sections.architecture: Solar geometry and irradiance feed a single-diode PV model (about 4.8 W peak at solar noon). The power chain runs through a CN3791 charger, Li-ion protection, an SOC estimator and a boost stage to 5 V. Position control and INA219 sensing close the loop.
sections.circuit: CN3791 charger, DW01A battery protection with an FS8205A MOSFET, MT3608 boost converter to 5 V, and an INA219 for monitoring.
sections.pcb: A 2-layer PCB with an ATmega328P as the controller.
sections.testing: Verified in simulation at the model-in-the-loop stage. Planned next: sensor non-idealities, a Stateflow perturb-and-observe tracker, a 12-hour comparison against a fixed panel, and PIL/HIL code generation.
sections.results: A working Simulink model of the power chain and tracking control, and a completed PCB design. Hardware validation has not been done yet.

title: Temperature-Controlled DC Fan Board
summary: An STM32 board that reads temperature and drives a 12 V fan, powered from a single 20 to 25 V input with 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V rails on board.

image.alt: 3D render of the temperature-controlled fan board

status: Schematic and layout complete. Firmware not yet written.

sections.overview: A compact controller built around an STM32F411CEU6. It measures ambient temperature with a TMP36 and sets a 12 V DC fan's speed by switching an AO3400A MOSFET with PWM. The design is split into Power, MCU, Sensor and Actuator sheets in Altium Designer.
sections.architecture: A 20 to 25 V DC barrel jack feeds two synchronous buck converters (TPS563300 and TPS54202) for the 12 V and 5 V rails, and an AMS1117-3.3 LDO for the 3.3 V rail.
sections.circuit: The TMP36 analog output goes to the STM32 ADC. A PWM output drives the AO3400A N-channel MOSFET, with flyback protection across the fan.
sections.pcb: Designed in Altium Designer. See the top-layer layout and 3D renders below.
components: TPS563300 and TPS54202 synchronous buck converters
sections.firmware: Not written yet. The plan is ADC sampling of the TMP36, a temperature-to-duty-cycle curve and PWM fan control.
sections.testing: The LTspice simulation shows 18.5 mV of output ripple on the buck converter. The repository includes the BOM and a bring-up plan. Before connecting a fan or flashing firmware, check polarity and verify the 12 V and 3.3 V rails.
sections.results: Schematic and layout are complete. Gerber export, fabrication and firmware are next.

title: CORE-328PB Microcontroller Module
summary: A solder-down ATmega328PB module with USB-UART programming, a source-OR-ed power path and 26 castellated I/O pads.

sections.overview: A compact module built around the ATmega328PB (32-pin VFQFN), programmed over micro-USB. It exposes 26 castellated edge pads (D0 to D13, A0 to A7, AREF, +5V, VCC and GND) so it can be soldered onto a carrier board.
sections.architecture: Power comes from USB through a Schottky OR-ing diode, or from an unregulated VCC pad regulated by an LM1117-5.0. An FT232RL USB-UART bridge programs the chip, with DTR-driven auto-reset.
sections.pcb: A two-sided board: the MCU, crystal, reset switch, status LEDs and USB connector on top, and the FT232RL, LM1117 and tantalum capacitor on the bottom.
components: Schottky OR-ing diode for USB and external power
challenges: The castellated reset pad was replaced with an on-board reset pushbutton.
Rev A review notes are tracked in the repository. Rev B is planned to expose RESET and more ATmega328PB peripherals.
sections.firmware: Programmed over micro-USB through the FT232RL, with DTR-driven auto-reset.
sections.results: Rev A is fabricated. Bring-up is the next step.

title: 7-Output Power Supply
summary: An isolated flyback with buck stages behind it, giving fixed and adjustable rails from one board.

sections.overview: An isolated flyback converter followed by buck stages. The fixed rails are +5, +12 and +24 V at 1 to 2 A, and two further rails are adjustable (+24 V and −12 V).

title: Dual-Motor H-Bridge Driver
summary: A MOSFET driver for motor direction and speed, on a 2-layer board that was fabricated and tested.

sections.overview: A MOSFET H-bridge driver that controls the direction and speed of two motors. A 2-layer board, fabricated and tested.

title: Assistive Lower-Limb Exoskeleton
summary: His B.Sc. graduation project: a fully built, working exoskeleton, built by a team of 6 under his lead.
status: Fully built and working. Grade: Excellent.

sections.overview: The graduation project for his B.Sc. in Mechatronics Engineering. He led a team of 6 to build a working assistive lower-limb exoskeleton.
sections.architecture: A galvanized sheet-metal frame carries NEMA 17 motors with custom spur gearboxes. A RISC-V controller reads gyroscope and limit-switch feedback.
components: NEMA 17 motors with custom spur gearboxes
sections.results: The system is fully built and working. Grade: Excellent.
